title: Offline Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning-based Recommendation: A Critical Issue and Some Alternatives
reasoning: The paper discusses 'beyond-accuracy goals' for recommender systems such as diversity, novelty, serendipity, fairness, and user experience, which have ethical implications. However, the core focus of the paper is on the technical shortcomings of existing offline evaluation protocols for RL-based recommenders (specifically next-item prediction) and proposing alternative technical evaluation methodologies to better reflect the long-term benefits and technical deficiencies of RL. It does not perform an explicit evaluation or benchmarking of moral, religious, or ethical dimensions of the RL systems themselves, but rather the adequacy of evaluation methods to capture intended system behaviors (which may include aspects like fairness as a desired outcome).
